sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17. Quoted: 'For read-write workloads, use <fog-name>.database.windows.net as the server name in the connection string'; read-only '<fog-name>.secondary.database.windows.net'; listeners 'remain unchanged during geo-failovers. You don't have to change the connection string ... connections are automatically routed to the current primary'; listener DNS TTL 30 seconds; failover performs full synchronization with no data loss and needs the primary accessible; forced failover 'immediately switches the secondary to the primary role without waiting for recent changes to propagate'. The page (read 2026-11-18) says to use the failover group's listener ('Connections are automatically directed to the primary. This name doesn't change after failover'); a server's own name stays with that server, which becomes the secondary after a failover. The read-only error text is an authored rendering.

brief.situation: You are the database administrator at Haldane Freight. During last night's East US outage the on-call DBA failed over the failover group fog-ops at 02:40; sql-ops-wus (West US) is now primary. East US recovered at 06:20, and sql-ops-eus is back as the readable secondary. Since 06:25 the warehouse order service fails every write. The warehouse shift starts picking at 08:00.
handover: Most services connect through fog-ops.database.windows.net; the order service was built by a contractor.
Failing back to East US is planned for Saturday's window, as a normal (no data loss) failover.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the failover group's listeners, the two servers' current roles and where each service connects.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

writeup.question: For the record: why writes failed after the region recovered, what you changed, and why not fail back now.

parts.label: Why
parts.criteria: Connects the role change to the connection string.
parts.modelAnswer: After the 02:40 failover West is primary. order-svc's connection string named sql-ops-eus directly; when East recovered as the readable secondary, order-svc reached it and every write failed as read-only.

parts.label: Change
parts.modelAnswer: Pointed order-svc at fog-ops.database.windows.net, the read-write listener that always routes to the current primary, and restarted it; a test order was written on West.

parts.label: Not now
parts.modelAnswer: A forced failover back would skip synchronization and lose West's latest orders, and interrupt every service at shift start. Failback is planned for Saturday as a normal failover, and deployments now reject member server names.

expertPath.text: West primary, East secondary; order-svc names sql-ops-eus; read-only errors; only order-svc bypasses the listener.
Connection string to fog-ops listener, restart; deploy check; failback stays planned for Saturday.

ordersLost.headline: Move the app, not the database
ordersLost.body: Forced failover is for when the primary is unreachable. Here the primary was healthy; the app pointed at the wrong server. Use the listener, and fail back later with a planned, synchronized failover.

pickingStopped.headline: Server names do not follow failovers
pickingStopped.body: A failover group's listener moves with the primary role; a member server's own name does not. Applications should connect to the listener.

onListener.headline: Good: fixed the connection, kept the data
onListener.body: You read the roles and the connection string, moved the service to the read-write listener instead of moving the database, checked a test order, and guarded the deployments.

gaps.headline: Held, with gaps
gaps.body: The criteria show what was left: the evidence before the change, the lasting step, the check, or the cause in the record.

time_up.headline: Time up
time_up.body: No record was written before the run's hard limit.

scoring.modelReasoning: The failover group is healthy with West primary; the order service named the East server directly, so when East returned as the readable secondary its writes failed. Point it at the read-write listener, which follows the primary role, and check a test order. A forced failback would skip synchronization and lose recent orders; a restart reconnects to the same name. Then block member-server names in deployments and fail back in the planned window.
